Can you confirm how Redwood counts tokens in the following scenarios for the hosted API baseline (no reserved commit yet):

1) System prompt included in API payload (single system prompt at session start) + user messages after that. Is the system prompt charged on every request or amortized somehow?
2) Streaming generation where the model emits tool call tokens mid-stream (we call multiple tools sequentially in a single request). Are tool-call tokens billed as output tokens at the time they are emitted, and how does rounding work when a stream yields partial tokens over multiple flushes?
3) When we wrap the same system prompt into a cached KV for subsequent calls, does Redwood's meter count the system prompt as input tokens for the first request only or for every rehydration?

We attached a tiny example payload (acme_example_payloads.json) with three short requests that mix system prompt, tool calls and streaming. Please return token math we can paste into our SOW. Also advise whether there are any rounding edge cases (per-request roundup to nearest token, per-stream chunk rounding, etc.) that could materially affect cost at scale.

Appreciate a concise response today if possible.

Samantha —

Thanks for the clear examples and the file. High level answers first, then Karthik will add the precise token math and edge-case examples.

High level:
- System prompts: charged as input tokens on every API request by default. If you use Redwood's prefix/KV cache (we showed this in the demo) and the prompt is served from cache without re-sending the full prompt, billing treats the cached prompt as amortized; the first request that pins the cache is charged the full prompt, subsequent cache hits are charged a small rehydration delta (if any).
- Tool calls in streaming: tool-call tokens are counted as output tokens at the time they are emitted. We perform per-request token rounding to the next whole token; streaming flushes do not create additional rounding beyond the final output tokenization.
- Rounding: our hosted baseline rounds per-request totals up to the nearest token. We do not round per-chunk in a way that double-charges the same partial token. That said, certain compatibility modes (legacy streaming protocols) can cause minor discrepancies — Karthik will enumerate those.

I've attached sample_ratecard_v2.pdf which includes baseline hosted rates and discount breakpoints (for reference only). We'll follow up with precise examples and a short table of how the three payloads from your file will be billed.

Next steps: Karthik — can you add the worked token math for Samantha's three sample requests and call out the caching/rehydration math? Marissa — please confirm whether we can offer a one-time POC credit for Acme while they validate the model behavior.

Samantha — adding the worked examples below. I kept them short and numbered to match your payload file. These assume our hosted baseline (no enterprise reserved commit) and standard tokenizer matching the open model we demonstrated.

Example A (single request, system prompt included, no cache)
- System prompt length: 48 tokens
- User message: 12 tokens
- Model output (final): 86 tokens
- Billing: input = system(48) + user(12) = 60 input tokens -> output = 86 tokens
- Rounding: per-request totals are rounded up per side; inputs 60 -> 60 (already whole), outputs 86 -> 86
- Total billed tokens for request A = 146 tokens (charged at input and output unit rates per ratecard).

Example B (single request, streaming with tool calls)
- System prompt length: 48 tokens (included in payload)
- User message: 7 tokens
- Streaming output sequence (emitted chunks):
  * chunk 1: "Analysis: ..." -> tokenized to 14 tokens (emitted)
  * tool call (call payload emitted inline): tool call token sequence -> 18 tokens emitted
  * model resumes and emits final text: 32 tokens
- How we bill: tool-call tokens are treated as model output tokens at emission time. We tokenize the final assembled output for billing purposes and count each output token once. Internally we flush stream chunks for client delivery, but we do not double-count partially emitted tokens across flushes.
- Rounding: suppose a flush emitted a partial byte sequence that tokenizes to 0.8 of a token (rare); we do not bill 0.8 then bill again when remaining bytes arrive. We bill based on tokenizer boundaries; final requested output = 14 + 18 + 32 = 64 output tokens -> round up to 64.
- Billing math: input = 48 + 7 = 55 input tokens; output = 64 tokens -> total 119 tokens billed.

Example C (cache rehydration case, repeat call)
- First call (warm): system prompt sent and cached: charged as normal (system 48 + user 10 + output 40 = 98 tokens).
- Subsequent cache hit: when the client uses the cached prefix, the API call payload can omit the full system prompt; Redwood performs a rehydration delta (we may send a small fingerprint/handle). We charge a small rehydration delta (typically 0-3 tokens) to account for the metadata footprint. In practice we measure this per-request delta and include it as input tokens.
- Note: if a customer explicitly re-sends the full system prompt each time, it's charged every time (no automatic deduplication on server side unless you opt into Redwood prefix/KV cache feature).

Legacy/edge cases to flag:
- Older streaming clients that repeatedly re-open sub-streams can create additional API requests; each request is billed separately, and that can raise costs.
- Very short outputs (1-2 tokens) still get tokenized normally; the per-request rounding up to the next whole token means micro-requests have a non-zero minimum cost.
- Tool-call tokens are always billed as output; tool execution itself (if we call customer-owned tooling) may have separate infra charges but not in your baseline hosted ratecard.

Summary table (quick):
- System prompt: charged per request unless cached via prefix/KV (first request charged in full; subsequent hits charge rehydration delta)
- Streaming tool tokens: billed as output at emission time, tokenizer-boundary accounting ensures no double-counting across flushes
- Rounding: per-request rounding to whole tokens; no per-flush double rounding
